_readme: Sources actually pulled from for the Wave 2 / Agent E torsion-knowledge PR (feat/3d-torsion-knowledge-v2). Every RDKit file below was fetched read-only via `curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rdkit/rdkit/<pinned_commit>/<path>` and hashed with `shasum -a 256` -- never rendered/paraphrased from a webpage. No RDKit code was compiled, linked, or executed; only its plain-text C++/.in data files were read as a reference oracle for translation and provenance labeling.

rdkit_oracle.note: Same RDKit release the sibling gap-check example (distance_geometry_v2_gap_check.rs) already cites as its oracle (RDKit 2025.09.2), kept consistent across the 3D Breakthrough Program's Wave 1/2 fixtures rather than picking a different pin. This is a SOURCE-FILE pin (read-only .in/.cpp text, never compiled/executed) used for translation provenance -- see `live_oracle_for_wave2_gap_fixes` below for the separate, later, LIVE-BEHAVIORAL RDKit oracle used for spec section 12's differential, which is a different RDKit artifact entirely and intentionally not forced to the same version.

live_oracle_for_wave2_gap_fixes.purpose: spec section 12's live RDKit oracle differential (ring classification + empirical torsion distribution), run during a post-independent-review fix pass on this same PR, distinct from the source-file pin above.
live_oracle_for_wave2_gap_fixes.environment: Isolated venv created via `python3 -m venv`, RDKit installed via `pip install rdkit` from PyPI -- never this repo's shared `.venv`, per this program's standing rule.
live_oracle_for_wave2_gap_fixes.note: Deliberately NOT pinned to Release_2025_09_2 -- pip's rdkit package tracks its own PyPI release cadence, independent of the GitHub source tag used for translation provenance. Using whatever the isolated venv resolves to (rather than trying to force a matching build) is consistent with section 12's own framing ("compare... not exact coordinates"): the comparison targets are ring-perception/torsion-distribution BEHAVIOR, which is far more stable across RDKit minor versions than exact numeric coefficients would be.
live_oracle_for_wave2_gap_fixes.summary: See docs/3d_torsion_knowledge_audit.md section 6 for the full writeup, corrected after independent review found the rule-family/1-4-pair differential IS achievable (rdDistGeom.GetExperimentalTorsions / GetMoleculeBoundsMatrix -- see the Wrap/rdDistGeom.cpp source entry above): (1) ring classification 221/230 (96.1%) agreement across 24 fixtures, all 9 disagreements in cubane, an expected pre-existing chematic design difference (augmented_ring_set recovering a real extra small ring SSSR's minimum basis omits), not a bug; (2) RDKit's own ETKDG conformer ensemble empirically confirms this PR's secondary-amide rule's predicted 180-degree minimum; (3) rule-family/central-bond-selection: chematic assigns a torsion to 194 bonds vs RDKit's 274 across all 72 knowledge-layer fixtures, 160 shared, 142/160 (88.8%) chose the IDENTICAL atom quadruple (up from 126/160=78.8% before two real bugs this differential itself found were fixed: a missing outer-atom ring-membership constraint in rules_smallring.rs's generic rules, and the atom-order/uniquify bug in matcher.rs) -- the residual 18 mismatches concentrate in fused-ring-junction bonds (steroid ring fusions in testosterone/cholesterol, penicillin's beta-lactam/thiazolidine fusion, aspirin's aryl ester), a known, disclosed translation-coarseness gap, not chased further; (4) macrocycle 1-4 pairs: RDKit's useMacrocycle14config flag only changes bounds-matrix entries for amide-context macrocycle bonds (0 pairs changed for pure-hydrocarbon/crown-ether macrocycles, 12-15 for the two macrolactam fixtures, 2 overlapping chematic's own broader proposal each time) -- a genuine, disclosed SCOPE difference: chematic proposes adjustments for every macrocycle 1-4 pair (relaxing non-amide ones to a wide band), RDKit's flag apparently only touches the amide/ester-pinned subset, non-amide macrocycle 1-4 bounds evidently already matching between the flag's two settings without needing the flag.

primary_literature.citation: Riniker, S.; Landrum, G. A. "Better Informed Distance Geometry: Using What We Know To Improve Conformation Generation." J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2015, 55 (12), 2562-2574.
primary_literature.access_method: Not fetched as full text (paywalled, no venv/network access to the publisher in this environment). Cross-verified indirectly: RDKit's own shipped `torsionPreferencesV1`/`torsionPreferencesV2` data tables (fetched below) are literally the artifact this paper describes -- their in-source header comments cite the same paper lineage ("J. Med. Chem. 56, 1026-2028 (2013)" for v1, "J. Chem. Inf. Model. 56, 1 (2016)" for v2 -- the v2 citation in RDKit's own comment differs slightly in year/volume from the DOI above; recorded verbatim as RDKit states it, not corrected against the paper, since the paper itself was not directly read). This is a real, disclosed limitation: the paper's methodology is understood second-hand through its operational implementation, not first-hand from the text. See `docs/3d_torsion_knowledge_audit.md` for how this affects the independent-vs-adapted classification of each rule.

primary_literature.citation: Wang, S.; Witek, J.; Landrum, G. A.; Riniker, S. "Improving Conformer Generation for Small Rings and Macrocycles Based on Distance Geometry and Experimental Torsional-Angle Preferences." J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2020, 60 (4), 2044-2058.
primary_literature.access_method: Not fetched as full text (paywalled). Cross-verified indirectly: `torsionPreferences_smallrings.in` and `torsionPreferences_macrocycles.in` (fetched below) both carry an in-source header comment citing this exact DOI verbatim -- confirmed by direct read of the fetched bytes, not assumed.
algorithmic_facts_recovered_from_source_: MIN_MACROCYCLE_SIZE = 9 (small ring vs macrocycle boundary) -- from TorsionPreferences.cpp line 35.
compute14DistCis/compute14DistTrans law-of-cosines-style geometric construction for macrocycle 1-4 bound relaxation -- from Geometry/Utils.h.

Macrocycle 1-4 relaxation logic: for a B-C bond fully inside one macrocycle ring, both the cis (compute14DistCis) and trans (compute14DistTrans) 1-4 distances are accepted as a WIDE band (min/max of both) UNLESS the B-C-A angle sequence matches an amide/ester pattern (_checkMacrocycleAllInSameRingAmideEster14 / _checkMacrocycleTwoInSameRingAmideEster14), in which case the amide/ester bond is still pinned to a single (cis) configuration with a tight +/-GEN_DIST_TOL band -- from BoundsMatrixBuilder.cpp lines ~1232-1440.

rdkit_source_files.used_for: Confirms the 4 real RDKit flag names this PR's TorsionKnowledgeConfig mirrors: useExpTorsions, useSmallRingTorsions, useMacrocycleTorsions, useBasicKnowledge (getExperimentalTorsions signature).

MIN_MACROCYCLE_SIZE=9 constant; fused/bridged-ring bond exclusion logic (excludedBonds bitset, numBondRings(bid2)>3 check) translated into this PR's BondClassification::FusedOrBridged reasoning; useBasicKnowledge flat-ring (4-6-membered, all-sp2 atoms) 2-fold torsion rule, translated into rules_basic.rs's flat_ring_rule.

calcTorsionEnergyM6: confirms the Fourier energy form E = sum_{n=1..6} V_n*(1+s_n*cos(n*phi)) and its analytic dE/dphi, translated into FourierTorsionTerm::energy/d_energy_d_phi_deg. Independent re-derivation in Rust (not transliterated line-for-line: RDKit expands cos(n*phi) via Chebyshev recurrences in cos(phi) for a Cartesian-gradient force field; this PR's optimizer works directly in torsion-angle space, so `f64::cos`/`f64::sin` of n*phi are used directly -- see PR body for why this is a deliberate simplification, not an oversight).
Signature reference only, no data taken.
Confirms how CrystalFFDetails terms are registered as ForceField contribs; not otherwise reused (this PR does not build a Cartesian ForceFieldContrib; see optimize_torsions doc comment).

Standard experimental torsion data table ("J. Med. Chem. 56, 1026-2028 (2013)" per RDKit's own header comment). NOT reproduced wholesale -- a curated subset (see rules_standard.rs's SOURCE_LINE comments, each citing an exact 1-based line number in this fetched file) was translated verbatim (SMARTS text + V/sign coefficients unchanged) into StandardExperimental rules. Rules not selected are NOT implemented, NOT counted, and NOT claimed as covered.

Standard experimental torsion data table, version 2 ("J. Chem. Inf. Model. 56, 1 (2016)" per RDKit's own header comment -- this is RDKit's default ETversion=2, matching what this PR's rules_standard.rs draws its curated subset from). Same non-wholesale-reproduction caveat as v1 above.

Small-ring experimental torsion data table, header cites doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.0c00025 verbatim. Uses RDKit-only SMARTS extensions chematic-smarts does not implement (`r{5-8}` ring-size RANGE syntax; chematic's own `rN` primitive is single-digit-exact only, see crates/chematic-smarts/src/parser.rs's own doc comment). Rules were therefore ADAPTED, not transliterated: the connectivity/hybridization part of each chosen SMARTS was kept, the `r{a-b}` ring-size qualifier was replaced with an explicit Rust-side ring-size-bucket check against this PR's own classify.rs ring classification. V/sign coefficients for the chosen subset were kept as fetched, byte-for-byte, from this file.
Macrocycle experimental torsion data table, header cites doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.0c00025 verbatim. Same `r{9-}` range-syntax adaptation caveat as smallrings.in above (ring-size >=9 check moved to Rust).

Confirms the exact flag name useMacrocycle14config (maps 1:1 to this PR's/EmbedParameters' use_macrocycle_14_bounds) and its documented semantics ("If 1-4 distances bound heuristics for macrocycles is used"). Also surfaces forceTransAmides (default true, no chematic equivalent exists yet) -- recorded as a known gap in docs/3d_torsion_knowledge_audit.md, not silently absorbed into this PR's scope.
Read for context on how useMacrocycle14config feeds into the real embedder call graph (confirms it flows into BoundsMatrixBuilder's set14Bounds, not a separate code path). No data/coefficients taken.

Real macrocycle 1-4 bounds algorithm, translated into bounds14.rs: minMacrocycleRingSize=9 (line 36); _checkMacrocycleTwoInSameRingAmideEster14/_checkMacrocycleAllInSameRingAmideEster14 amide/ester detection (lines ~887-1243, used verbatim as the amide/ester-vs-generic branch condition, re-expressed against chematic_core::Molecule instead of RDKit's ROMol); _setMacrocycleTwoInSameRing14Bounds/_setMacrocycleAllInSameRing14Bounds 'assume anything is possible' cis-or-trans wide-band relaxation for non-amide macrocycle 1-4 pairs (lines ~1245-1440); set14Bounds's useMacrocycle14config gating (lines ~1519-1610).
Read for context (ETKDGv3 default construction), not otherwise reused.

compute13Dist/compute14DistCis/compute14DistTrans -- exact law-of-cosines-in-a-rotated-plane geometric formulas, translated near-verbatim (same algorithm, same variable roles, re-typed for chematic_core) into bounds14.rs's dist13/dist14_cis/dist14_trans. Copyright (C) 2004-2006 Rational Discovery LLC, BSD-3-Clause (see attribution note below).

Fetched during a post-independent-review fix pass, NOT during the original translation work: this is the pybind wrapper that exposes `GetExperimentalTorsions` (lines 316/324) and `GetMoleculeBoundsMatrix` (line 660) to Python. An earlier draft of this PR claimed the rule-family/1-4-pair-selection differential spec section 12 asks for was 'not achievable via RDKit's public API' after reading only `DistGeomHelpers/{Embedder,BoundsMatrixBuilder,EmbedderUtils}.{h,cpp}` above -- never `DistGeomHelpers/Wrap/`, where the actual Python accessors live. That claim was corrected after independent review pointed at this exact file/these exact line numbers; verified here by fetching and re-reading it directly, not by trusting the correction at face value. Not used for translation (these two functions are called live via the isolated venv, not ported into Rust) -- recorded here purely as the source-provenance evidence for why the differential in docs/3d_torsion_knowledge_audit.md section 6 is now real, not merely asserted possible.

license_note.rdkit_license: BSD-3-Clause (per RDKit's own file headers: 'The contents are covered by the terms of the BSD license which is included in the file license.txt, found at the root of the RDKit source tree.')
license_note.attribution_applied: Every Rust source file in crates/chematic-3d/src/etkdg_knowledge/ that translates or adapts RDKit data/algorithms carries a doc comment citing: (a) the RDKit file path and commit this manifest pins, (b) the original RDKit copyright line as it appears in the fetched file header, (c) whether the specific rule/function is a verbatim data translation, an algorithm re-derivation, or an adaptation with a stated difference. This satisfies BSD-3-Clause's attribution/copyright-notice-preservation requirement without redistributing RDKit source files themselves (only specific numeric coefficients and short SMARTS strings -- data, not copyrightable expression of substantial code -- plus short, attributed paraphrases of the geometric formulas).

independent_implementations_derived_from: TorsionKnowledgeConfig/TorsionPotential/FourierTorsionTerm/TorsionKnowledgeReport data model (crates/chematic-3d/src/etkdg_knowledge/types.rs) -- shape only, no RDKit source copied.

BondClassification / classify_bond (classify.rs) -- ring-size-bucket + fused/bridged/amide/aromatic/terminal tagging logic is this PR's own design, informed by (not copied from) TorsionPreferences.cpp's excludedBonds logic.

Priority-tier matcher (matcher.rs) -- the exact 6-tier ordering (specific validated SMARTS > small-ring > macrocycle > standard > basic-knowledge > legacy) is a chematic-specific decision by the project owner's spec, NOT RDKit's own iteration order (RDKit's own getExperimentalTorsions loop is simple first-match-not-yet-done over the concatenated v2+smallrings+macrocycles string, giving STANDARD priority over small-ring/macrocycle in real RDKit -- this PR's ordering deliberately differs; see docs/3d_torsion_knowledge_audit.md and the PR body's judgment-call section).

optimize_torsions' torsion-space (not Cartesian force-field) rigid-fragment rotation optimizer -- this PR's own design, not a port of RDKit's ForceField machinery (which operates in Cartesian space via TorsionAngleContribM6::getGrad).
adapted_or_translated_from_rdkit: A curated subset of rules_standard.rs's StandardExperimental SMARTS + Fourier coefficients (verbatim data from torsionPreferences_v2.in, cited by exact line number per rule).

A curated, ring-size-range-adapted subset of rules_smallring.rs's SmallRingExperimental rules (SMARTS connectivity kept, `r{a-b}` range replaced by a Rust-side check; V/sign coefficients kept verbatim).
A curated, ring-size-range-adapted subset of rules_macrocycle.rs's MacrocycleAdaptation rules (same adaptation pattern as small-ring, `r{9-}` -> Rust-side check).
rules_basic.rs's flat 4-6-membered all-sp2-ring rule -- translated from TorsionPreferences.cpp's useBasicKnowledge block.

bounds14.rs's macrocycle_14_bound_adjustments -- dist13/dist14_cis/dist14_trans geometric formulas translated from Geometry/Utils.h; amide/ester-vs-generic branch and the cis-or-trans wide-band relaxation translated from BoundsMatrixBuilder.cpp's macrocycle-specific functions.
kept_as_is_legacy_reclassified_only: classify_atom_type, get_torsion_preference, build_smarts_torsion_map, default_torsion_preference, score_torsion (etkdg_knowledge.rs) -- behavior UNCHANGED. Only the module-level doc comment's false 'from CSD' claim is corrected, and the audit doc reclassifies each rule's real provenance (see docs/3d_torsion_knowledge_audit.md). No regression fixtures needed because output is byte-identical (no legacy function was made to internally delegate to the new v2 implementation).
